accepted.sentence: To start moving, the rider straddles the frame, places one foot on a pedal, pushes off, then begins pedaling.
On level ground, continued pedaling maintains motion, while stopping the effort allows the wheels to coast.
Before climbing a hill, the rider may select a lower gear, making each pedal stroke easier but slower.
Shifting gears is smoother when pedal pressure eases briefly as the chain moves between sprockets.
While turning, the rider steers through the curve and leans slightly to help maintain balance.
Applying both brakes progressively slows the vehicle and helps the rider maintain control on slippery pavement.
For a controlled stop, the rider reduces speed before placing one foot on the ground.
Before setting out, checking tire pressure and testing the brakes can reveal problems that affect safe handling.
